blocks.md: Group an unbounded event stream into finite event-time windows. Events update live aggregates; a watermark proves that older windows are complete, so they can be emitted once and forgotten.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: At watermark 10, Window 0 is final: emit api(count=2, sum=8) and evict it. Window 1 remains live.

blocks.title: Watermark means knowledge
blocks.md: A watermark at tick `t` says no future event belongs before `t` in this tier. It is not an event and it does not belong to a window; it closes every window whose end is at most `t`.

blocks.input:
WindowSize = 10
Event(tick=9, key=A, value=4)
Event(tick=10, key=A, value=7)
Watermark(10)
blocks.output:
emit [0,10): A count=1 sum=4
keep [10,20): A count=1 sum=7
blocks.explain: Windows are half-open. Tick 9 belongs to the first window; tick 10 starts the next. The watermark closes only the first.

items: Compute `start = floor(tick / WindowSize) * WindowSize` using safe integer arithmetic.
Emit each final key/window aggregate exactly once, in canonical record form.
Repeated or larger watermarks must not duplicate prior output.
Evict finalized state; `Close` emits every window still active.

items.title: Key state by window and key
items.md: Each event updates only one count and sum in one fixed window.

items.title: Finalize by end time
items.md: On a watermark, find windows with `end <= tick`, emit all their keys, then delete them.

items.title: Keep state proportional to the live horizon
items.md: Never retain the full input stream or already-finalized windows.

blocks.title: Why the metrics fit the model
blocks.md: Throughput rewards a small hot path; peak state checks timely eviction; output delay checks prompt finalization; allocation bytes reveal per-event churn.
